# 1 · Natural Spline Smoothing {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## Why Natural Splines (`ns()`)?

**Goal:** Extract the underlying trend from a noisy weekly WBE signal.

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Properties:**

-   Linear outside the boundary knots
-   Fits inside `lm()` — gives standard errors
-   Fast, interpretable, no extra dependencies
-   `df` argument controls flexibility directly

**Choosing `df`:**

-   Be cautious of over fitting and under fitting.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Key parameters in `ns()`:**

+------------------+----------------------------------------------+---------------------+
| Parameter        | Role                                         | Default             |
+==================+==============================================+=====================+
| `df`             | Total basis functions (= interior knots + 1) | Required            |
+------------------+----------------------------------------------+---------------------+
| `knots`          | Manual knot positions (overrides `df`)       | Auto from quantiles |
+------------------+----------------------------------------------+---------------------+
| `Boundary.knots` | Range limits; linear beyond these            | `range(x)`          |
+------------------+----------------------------------------------+---------------------+
| `intercept`      | Include intercept column in basis?           | `FALSE`             |
+------------------+----------------------------------------------+---------------------+
:::
:::

## Spline Specifications — `ns()` Internals

**Model fitted:**

$$y_t \;=\; \beta_0 + \sum_{j=1}^{\texttt{df}} \beta_j \, N_j(t) + \varepsilon_t, \qquad \varepsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2)$$

where $N_j(t)$ are the **natural cubic spline basis functions** from `splines::ns()`.

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Knot placement**

`ns()` places **interior knots** at equally-spaced quantiles of $t$ by default.

$$\text{interior knots} = \texttt{df} - 1$$

`df = 14` → **13 interior knots** placed at equally-spaced quantiles of `datepredict`.

**Boundary knots** are fixed at `min(t)` and `max(t)`.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Standard error derivation**

`predict(lm(...), se = TRUE)` returns the pointwise SE:

$$\widehat{\text{SE}}[\hat{y}_t] = \sqrt{\mathbf{n}_t^\top \; \widehat{\Sigma}_\beta \; \mathbf{n}_t}$$

where $\mathbf{n}_t$ is the basis row at time $t$ and $\widehat{\Sigma}_\beta = \hat{\sigma}^2 (X^\top X)^{-1}$ is the OLS covariance matrix.

**Ribbon on plots:** $\hat{y}_t \pm 1.96 \times \widehat{\text{SE}}[\hat{y}_t]$\
≈ 95% pointwise confidence band.
:::
:::

## `spline_function_general()`

```{r}
#| label: fn-spline

spline_function_general <- function(x_series, df) {
  # PURPOSE: Fit a natural cubic spline trend to a WBE time series and
  # return fitted values + pointwise SE for confidence ribbon plots.
  #
  # INPUTS
  #   x_series — 2-column data frame: col 1 = date, col 2 = log10 signal
  #   df       — spline degrees of freedom
  # OUTPUT
  #   x_series + two new columns: Spline (fit) and Spline_se (pointwise SE)

  x_series_names <- names(x_series)

  # Extract by position so the function works with any column names
  x           <- pull(x_series, names(x_series)[2])   # numeric signal (log10 copies/L)
  datepredict <- pull(x_series, names(x_series)[1])   # time index (date)

  # OLS with natural spline basis: lm() estimates the β coefficients
  # ns() builds the design matrix with df columns (one per basis function)
  fitall <- lm(x ~ ns(datepredict, df = df))

  # predict(se = TRUE) returns fit + SE from the OLS covariance matrix
  # suppressWarnings(): silence notes
  predall <- suppressWarnings(
    predict(fitall, newdata = list(date = x_series[[1]]), se = TRUE)
  )

  # Assemble output: original columns + spline fit + spline SE
  xout <- data.frame(datepredict, x, predall$fit, predall$se.fit)
  names(xout) <- c(x_series_names, "Spline", "Spline_se")

  return(xout)
}
```

::: callout-note
`Spline_se` is the **pointwise** SE — it reflects uncertainty in the mean trend, not in individual observations. Use it for the ribbon: `Spline ± 2 × Spline_se`.
:::

# 2 · State Space Model {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## State Space Model — FDT Formulation

The SSM separates the underlying true viral trend from measurement noise. The FDT state equation incorporates quadratic local trends, capturing acceleration and deceleration of viral concentration over time (Ensor et al. 2025).

**Observation equation**: $$y_t = Z \, \alpha_t + v_t, \quad v_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, H)$$

**State equation**: $$\alpha_{t+1} = T \, \alpha_t + R \, w_t, \quad w_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, Q)$$

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Matrices:**

$$Z = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad
T = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad
R = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Parameters estimated by MLE:**

| Parameter | Role                       |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| $Q$       | Process noise variance     |
| $H$       | Observation noise variance |

$Q$ and $H$ are estimated from the data via `fitSSM()`. No manual tuning required.

**Kalman filter outputs:**

-   `Xf` — filtered state (uses data up to time $t$; for real-time)
-   `Xs` — smoothed state (uses all data; for publication)
-   `Pf` — filtered variance
:::
:::

## `ssm_fdt()`

```{r}
#| label: fn-ssm

# build_model(): defines the SSM matrices (Local Linear Trend / FDT)
build_model <- function(y) {
  Z    <- matrix(c(1, 0),     1, 2)   # observation eq: extracts level from state
  Tmat <- matrix(c(2,-1,1,0), 2, 2)   # transition eq: encodes Δ²αₜ = wₜ
  R    <- matrix(c(1, 0),     2, 1)   # noise selector: disturbance enters level only
  Q    <- matrix(NA)                   # process noise variance → estimated by MLE
  H    <- matrix(NA)                   # observation noise variance → estimated by MLE
  KFAS::SSModel(y ~ -1 + SSMcustom(Z = Z, T = Tmat, R = R, Q = Q,
                  P1 = diag(1e6, 2), P1inf = diag(2)), H = H)
}

# ssm_fdt(): fits the model via MLE, runs Kalman filter + smoother
# INPUT:  y — numeric vector of log10 viral concentrations (may contain NAs)
# OUTPUT: list with filtered (Xf, Pf) and smoothed (Xs, Ps) state estimates
ssm_fdt <- function(y) {
  # Preserve original time series properties (start, frequency)
  strt <- stats::tsp(as.ts(y))[1]
  frq  <- stats::tsp(as.ts(y))[3]

  # Add tiny random noise (~1e-6) to avoid degenerate likelihoods
  # when repeated identical values create a flat likelihood surface
  y    <- ts(jitter(y), frequency = frq)
  if (length(y) < 20) stop("ssm_fdt requires >=20 observations")

  # fitSSM() estimates Q and H via MLE
  # inits: starting values for the optimizer, on the log scale (variances must be > 0)
  #   derived from var(diff(y)) — the empirical week-to-week variability
  fit <- KFAS::fitSSM(build_model(y),
           inits = c(log(var(diff(y), na.rm = TRUE) / 10),   # starting guess for log(Q)
                     log(var(diff(y), na.rm = TRUE) / 100)),  # starting guess for log(H)
           hessian = TRUE)

  # KFS() runs both the Kalman filter (forward pass) and smoother (backward pass)
  kfs <- KFAS::KFS(fit$model)

  # Return filtered and smoothed estimates as time series objects
  invisible(list(
    Xf = ts(kfs$att[, 1],      start = strt, frequency = frq), # filtered state mean
    Xs = ts(kfs$alphahat[, 1], start = strt, frequency = frq), # smoothed state mean
    Pf = ts(apply(kfs$Ptt[1,1,,drop=F], 2, c), start = strt, frequency = frq), # filtered variance
    Ps = ts(apply(kfs$V[1,1,,drop=F],   2, c), start = strt, frequency = frq)  # smoothed variance
  ))
}
```

# 3 · Plotting the Results {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## Synthetic Data — Generate & Run Pipeline

```{r}
#| label: synth-fn-defs
#| eval: true
#| echo: false

# Re-define functions here so they are available at eval time
# (the earlier slides use global eval: false to show code without running it)

handle_nondetects <- function(df, copies_col="copies",
                              lod_col="Detection", seed=2020061) {
  set.seed(seed)
  copies <- df[[copies_col]]; lod <- df[[lod_col]]
  zeroindex   <- copies == 0
  naindex     <- copies < lod;       naindex[is.na(naindex)]     <- TRUE
  naindex_hlf <- copies < lod * 0.5; naindex_hlf[is.na(naindex_hlf)] <- TRUE
  df$rfill <- 0; df$NDInd <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(df)))
    df$rfill[i] <- runif(1, lod[i]/2, lod[i])
  df[[copies_col]][naindex_hlf] <- df$rfill[naindex_hlf]
  df$NDInd[naindex] <- 1L; df$NDInd[naindex_hlf] <- 2L
  df$NDInd[zeroindex] <- 3L
  return(df)
}

spline_function_general <- function(x_series, df) {
  x_series_names <- names(x_series)
  x           <- pull(x_series, names(x_series)[2])
  datepredict <- pull(x_series, names(x_series)[1])
  fitall  <- lm(x ~ ns(datepredict, df = df))
  predall <- suppressWarnings(
    predict(fitall, newdata = list(date = x_series[[1]]), se = TRUE))
  xout <- data.frame(datepredict, x, predall$fit, predall$se.fit)
  names(xout) <- c(x_series_names, "Spline", "Spline_se")
  return(xout)
}

build_model <- function(y) {
  Z <- matrix(c(1,0),1,2); Tmat <- matrix(c(2,-1,1,0),2,2)
  R <- matrix(c(1,0),2,1); Q <- matrix(NA); H <- matrix(NA)
  KFAS::SSModel(y ~ -1 + SSMcustom(Z=Z, T=Tmat, R=R, Q=Q,
                                    P1=diag(1e6,2), P1inf=diag(2)), H=H)
}

ssm_fdt <- function(y) {
  strt <- stats::tsp(as.ts(y))[1]; frq <- stats::tsp(as.ts(y))[3]
  y    <- ts(jitter(y), frequency = frq)
  if (length(y) < 20) stop("ssm_fdt requires >=20 observations")
  fit <- KFAS::fitSSM(build_model(y),
                      inits=c(log(var(diff(y), na.rm=TRUE)/10),
                              log(var(diff(y), na.rm=TRUE)/100)),
                      hessian=TRUE)
  kfs <- KFAS::KFS(fit$model)
  invisible(list(
    Xf = ts(kfs$att[,1], start=strt, frequency=frq),
    Pf = ts(apply(kfs$Ptt[1,1,,drop=FALSE],2,c), start=strt, frequency=frq)))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: synth-generate-and-run
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

# Create final data

set.seed(42)
n <- 166  # ~3.2 years of weekly data
dates   <- seq(as.Date("2020-07-06"), by = "week", length.out = n)
t       <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
lod_cpl <- runif(n, 10, 250)

# Synthetic log₁₀ signal with seasonal structure + noise
signal <- pmin(pmax(3.2 + 1.2*t + sin(2*pi*t*2.5) + 0.5*sin(2*pi*t*6), 2), 6)
synthetic_df <- data.frame(date = dates, copies = 10^(signal + rnorm(n, 0, 0.2)),
                           Detection = lod_cpl)

# Force low-signal samples below LOD
nd_rows <- which(rbinom(n, 1, (1 - (signal - 2) / 4) * 0.20) == 1)
synthetic_df$copies[nd_rows] <- lod_cpl[nd_rows] * runif(length(nd_rows), 0.1, 0.45)

# Non-detects + missing weeks
synthetic_df <- handle_nondetects(synthetic_df)   # see Appendix
synthetic_df$tcopies_L <- log10(synthetic_df$copies)
set.seed(512)
miss <- sort(sample(n, round(n * 0.09)))
synthetic_df$tcopies_L[miss] <- NA
missing_dates <- dates[miss]

# Fit spline + SSM
spline_result <- spline_function_general(synthetic_df[, c("date","tcopies_L")], df = 13)
ssm_result    <- ssm_fdt(synthetic_df$tcopies_L)
synthetic_df$Xf <- as.numeric(ssm_result$Xf)
synthetic_df$Pf <- sqrt(as.numeric(ssm_result$Pf))
```

## Plot Anatomy — Layering Order

The key to a clean R Base plot is **layering**: each element is drawn *on top* of the previous one.

+------------+-----------------------+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| Layer      | Function              | What it draws                    | Why this order?                                |
+:==========:+=======================+==================================+================================================+
| 1          | `plot(..., type="n")` | Empty frame (axes, labels)       | Blank slate but also sets coordinate system up |
+------------+-----------------------+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| 2          | `rect()`              | Gray bars (missing weeks)        | Background — we want it behind everything      |
+------------+-----------------------+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| 3          | `abline()`            | LOD reference line               | Horizontal reference behind data               |
+------------+-----------------------+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| 4          | `polygon()`           | Confidence ribbons (spline, SSM) | Semi-transparent bands behind lines            |
+------------+-----------------------+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| 5          | `lines()`             | Trend lines (spline, SSM)        | On top of ribbons, behind points               |
+------------+-----------------------+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| 6          | `points()`            | Raw data + ND circles            | Always on top — never hidden                   |
+------------+-----------------------+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| 7          | `legend()`            | Legend                           | Last — floats above all content                |
+------------+-----------------------+----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------+

::: callout-important
Ordering matters. For example, if you draw points before ribbons, `polygon()` will cover the `points()`. **Recommended order: frame → background → ribbons → lines → points → legend.**
:::

## Step 1 — Empty Frame + Margins

```{r}
#| label: plot-step1
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

# par(mar = ...) controls margins: c(bottom, left, top, right) in lines
par(mar = c(4, 4.8, 2.5, 1.5), bg = "white")

# type = "n" → draws axes and labels but NO data points
# This gives us a blank canvas to layer elements in the correct order
plot(synthetic_df$date, synthetic_df$tcopies_L,   # ← Data points we will plot later
     type = "n",                                  # ← empty frame
     ylim = c(1.2, 6.8),                          # ← control y range
     xlab = "Date",
     ylab = expression(log[10]~"copies / L"),      # ← math notation
     main = "Synthetic WBE — Ciudad de Mexico")
```

**Key `par()` settings for WBE plots:**

+--------------+-------------------------+-----------------------+---------------------------------+
| Parameter    | Default                 | Our Plot              | Effect                          |
+==============+:=======================:+:=====================:+=================================+
| `mar`        | `c(5.1, 4.1, 4.1, 2.1)` | `c(4, 4.8, 2.5, 1.5)` | More room for y-axis label      |
|              |                         |                       |                                 |
|              |                         |                       | c(bottom, left, top, right)     |
+--------------+-------------------------+-----------------------+---------------------------------+
| `bg`         | `"white"`               | `"white"`             | Explicit for export consistency |
+--------------+-------------------------+-----------------------+---------------------------------+
| `las`        | `0`                     | `1`                   | Horizontal y-axis tick labels   |
+--------------+-------------------------+-----------------------+---------------------------------+
| `cex.axis`   | `1`                     | `0.85`                | Slightly smaller tick labels    |
+--------------+-------------------------+-----------------------+---------------------------------+

## Step 2 — Rectangles for Missing Weeks with `rect()`

```{r}
#| label: plot-missing-bars
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

# ── Draw gray bars AFTER plot() but BEFORE ribbons/lines ──────────────────
# rect(xleft, ybottom, xright, ytop) draws a filled rectangle
bar_half <- 3.5   # half-week in days → centers bar on the missing date
for (d in as.numeric(missing_dates)) {
  rect(d - bar_half, 1.2,           # left edge, bottom
       d + bar_half, 6.8,           # right edge, top (match ylim)
       col    = adjustcolor("grey70", alpha.f = 0.35),
       border = NA)                  # no outline
}
```

::: callout-note
`rect()` uses **data coordinates** (same units as your axes). For a weekly time series, `bar_half = 3.5` days makes each bar exactly one week wide.
:::

## Step 3 — Reference Lines

```{r}
#| label: plot-step2
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

# ── Horizontal LOD reference ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# abline(h = ...) draws a horizontal line at the given y value
# lty = 2 → dashed;  col = "grey45" → subtle;  lwd = 1 → thin
abline(h = log10(median(lod_cpl)), lty = 2, col = "grey45", lwd = 1)

# ── Text annotation near the line ─────────────────────────────────────────
# text() places a label at (x, y) coordinates in data units
# adj = 0 → left-aligned;  cex = 0.68 → small text
text(min(synthetic_df$date),                     # x = left edge of plot
     log10(median(lod_cpl)) + 0.12,            # y = slightly above the line
     sprintf("median LOD  (%.0f copies/L)", median(lod_cpl)),
     col = "grey45", cex = 0.68, adj = 0)
```

**Common `lty` (line type) values:**

| `lty` | Style    |
|:-----:|----------|
|   1   | Solid    |
|   2   | Dashed   |
|   3   | Dotted   |
|   4   | Dot-dash |

## Step 4 — Confidence Ribbons with `polygon()`

```{r}
#| label: plot-step3
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

# ── Spline ribbon ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# polygon() fills a closed region defined by x,y vertices
# Strategy: go forward along upper bound, then REVERSE along lower bound
polygon(
  x = c(spline_result$date, rev(spline_result$date)),   # forward, then back
  y = c(spline_result$Spline + 1.96*spline_result$Spline_se,  # upper bound
        rev(spline_result$Spline - 1.96*spline_result$Spline_se)),  # lower bound (reversed)
  col    = adjustcolor("steelblue", alpha.f = 0.13),  # ← semi-transparent fill
  border = NA)                                         # ← no outline

# ── SSM ribbon (same pattern, different color) ────────────────────────────
polygon(
  x = c(synthetic_df$date, rev(synthetic_df$date)),
  y = c(synthetic_df$Xf + 1.96*synthetic_df$Pf,
        rev(synthetic_df$Xf - 1.96*synthetic_df$Pf)),
  col    = adjustcolor("darkorange", alpha.f = 0.12),
  border = NA)
```

::: callout-tip
**`adjustcolor(col, alpha.f = ...)`** is the key to semi-transparent fills. 0 is fully transparent and 1 is not transparent. Values 0.10–0.15 for **`alpha.f`** work well for ribbons that don't obscure underlying layers.
:::

## Step 5 — Trend Lines

```{r}
#| label: plot-step4
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

# ── Spline trend line ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lines(spline_result$date, spline_result$Spline,
      col = "steelblue",   # color to match its ribbon
      lwd = 2.2,           # line width: 2–3 is visible without dominating
      lty = 2)             # dashed → differentiate from SSM solid line

# ── SSM filtered state ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lines(synthetic_df$date, synthetic_df$Xf,
      col = "darkorange",  # color to match its ribbon
      lwd = 2.1,           # match spline thickness
      lty = 1)             # solid → differentiate from spline line
```

**Choosing `lwd` (line width):**

|    `lwd`    | Our Plot                 |
|:-----------:|--------------------------|
|     1.0     | Reference lines, grid    |
|   1.5–2.0   | Secondary trends         |
| **2.0–2.5** | **Primary trend lines**  |
|    3.0+     | Too thick for most plots |

## Step 6 — Data Points + Non-Detect Markers

```{r}
#| label: plot-step5
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

# ── All observed data points ──────────────────────────────────────────────
points(synthetic_df$date, synthetic_df$tcopies_L,
       pch = 16,            # filled circle
       col = "grey25",      # pick any color!
       cex = 0.75)          # smaller than default

# ── Non-detect circles overlaid ───────────────────────────────────────────
nd_flag <- synthetic_df$NDInd %in% c(1L, 2L, 3L)
points(synthetic_df$date[nd_flag], synthetic_df$tcopies_L[nd_flag],
       pch = 1,             # open circle → rings around the filled point
       col = "firebrick",   # red stands out
       cex = 1.6,           # larger than the data point it encircles
       lwd = 1.7)           # ring thickness
```

**Common `pch` (point character) values:**

| `pch` | Shape           | Could use for             |
|:-----:|-----------------|---------------------------|
|  16   | Filled circle   | Raw data (default)        |
|   1   | Open circle     | Highlighting (ND markers) |
|  15   | Filled square   | Category markers          |
|  17   | Filled triangle | Alternate group           |
|   4   | × (cross)       | Outliers                  |

## Step 7 — Legend Construction

```{r}
#| label: plot-step6
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

legend("topleft",          # position: "topleft", "topright", "bottomleft", etc.
       bty = "n",          # no box around the legend
       cex = 0.78,         # slightly smaller text
       legend = c("Raw signal", 
                  "Non-detect (circled)", 
                  "Missing week",
                  "Spline ± 1.96SE", 
                  "SSM filtered state ± 1.96SD"),
       col = c("grey25", "firebrick", adjustcolor("grey70", 0.55),
               "steelblue", "darkorange"),
       pch = c(16, 1, 15, NA, NA),    # points for data; NA for line-only entries
       lty = c(NA, NA, NA, 2, 1),     # lines for trends; NA for point-only entries
       lwd = c(NA, NA, NA, 2.2, 2.4),
       pt.cex = c(1, 1.3, 1.8, NA, NA))
```

::: callout-tip
**Mixing points and lines in one legend:** use `NA` for the `pch` of line-only entries, and `NA` for the `lty` of point-only entries. R draws only the non-NA element for each row.
:::

## Complete Plot

```{r}
#| label: synth-plot-missing
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.2

## Empty Frame
par(mar = c(4, 4.8, 2.5, 1.5), bg = "white")
ylims <- c(1.2, 6.8) # Set y-axis limit

plot(synthetic_df$date, synthetic_df$tcopies_L, type = "n", ylim = ylims,
     xlab = "Date", ylab = expression(log[10]~"copies / L"),
     main = "Synthetic WBE — Ciudad de Mexico  |  Missing weeks flagged")

## Missing weeks rectangles
bar_half <- 3.5
for (d in as.numeric(missing_dates)) {
  rect(d - bar_half, ylims[1], d + bar_half, ylims[2],
       col = adjustcolor("grey70", alpha.f = 0.35), border = NA)
}

## Reference line
abline(h = log10(median(lod_cpl)), lty = 2, col = "grey45", lwd = 1)
text(min(synthetic_df$date), log10(median(lod_cpl)) + 0.12,
     sprintf("median LOD  (%.0f copies/L)", median(lod_cpl)),
     col = "grey45", cex = 0.68, adj = 0)

## CI Ribbons
polygon(c(spline_result$date, rev(spline_result$date)),
        c(spline_result$Spline + 1.96*spline_result$Spline_se,
          rev(spline_result$Spline - 1.96*spline_result$Spline_se)),
        col = adjustcolor("steelblue", 0.13), border = NA)
polygon(c(synthetic_df$date, rev(synthetic_df$date)),
        c(synthetic_df$Xf + 1.96*synthetic_df$Pf,
          rev(synthetic_df$Xf - 1.96*synthetic_df$Pf)),
        col = adjustcolor("darkorange", 0.12), border = NA)

## Spline and SSM Trend lines
lines(spline_result$date, spline_result$Spline, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.2, lty = 2)
lines(synthetic_df$date, synthetic_df$Xf, col = "darkorange", lwd = 2.2)

## Data points - Copies/L
points(synthetic_df$date, synthetic_df$tcopies_L, pch = 16, col = "grey25", cex = 0.75)

## Circle ND
nd_flag <- !is.na(synthetic_df$NDInd) & synthetic_df$NDInd %in% c(1L, 2L, 3L)
points(synthetic_df$date[nd_flag], synthetic_df$tcopies_L[nd_flag],
       pch = 1, col = "firebrick", cex = 1.6, lwd = 1.7)

## Legend
legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.78,
       legend = c("Raw signal", "Non-detect (circled)", "Missing week",
                  "Spline ± 1.96SE", "SSM filtered state ± 1.96SD"),
       col = c("grey25", "firebrick", adjustcolor("grey70", 0.55),
               "steelblue", "darkorange"),
       pch = c(16, 1, 15, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, NA, NA, 2, 1),
       lwd = c(NA, NA, NA, 2.2, 2.4), pt.cex = c(1, 1.3, 1.8, NA, NA))
```

# Summary {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## Key Takeaways

::: incremental
**Estimates**

-   **The spline gives a global smooth trend with SEs.** The SE column enables confidence ribbons. Adjust `df` to match your data.

-   **The SSM estimates the underlying trend via the Kalman filter.** It separates process noise ($Q$) from observation noise ($H$) via MLE.

**Plotting in R Base Plots**

-   **Layering order matters for plots.** Frame → background → ribbons → lines → points → legend. Use `adjustcolor()` for semi-transparency.
:::

# Appendix {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## Pipeline at a Glance

```{r}
#| label: pipeline-summary
#| eval: false

# ── 1. Handle non-detects ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
df <- handle_nondetects(df, copies_col = "copies", lod_col = "Detection")
df$tcopies_L <- log10(df$copies)

# ── 2. Spline smooth ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
spline_result <- spline_function_general(df[, c("date","tcopies_L")], df = 30)

# ── 3. State space model ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
ssm_result <- ssm_fdt(df$tcopies_L)
df$Xf <- as.numeric(ssm_result$Xf)       # filtered state (log10 scale)
df$Pf <- sqrt(as.numeric(ssm_result$Pf)) # filtered SD → ribbon width ±2·Pf
```

::: callout-important
**Key column conventions**

+-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------+
| Column      | Content                                                        |
+=============+================================================================+
| `copies`    | Raw copies/L (linear); modified in-place by ND imputation      |
+-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------+
| `Detection` | Per-sample LOD in copies/L                                     |
+-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------+
| `NDInd`     | Non-detect flag: 0 = OK, 1 = below LOD, 2 = replaced, 3 = zero |
+-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------+
| `tcopies_L` | log₁₀ copies/L after imputation                                |
+-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------+
| `Xf`        | SSM filtered state (log₁₀ scale)                               |
+-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------+
| `Pf`        | SSM filtered SD — use for ±2 SD ribbons                        |
+-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------+
:::

## Non-Detect Handling — Why It Matters

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Our approach:** Probabilistic substitution with U(LOD/2, LOD) (U = Uniform Distribution)
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
+----------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
| Approach                         | Problem                             |
+==================================+=====================================+
| Drop the sample                  | A non-detect is *not* missing data  |
+----------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
| Substitute `LOD/2` (fixed)       | Ignores per-sample LOD variation    |
+----------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
| Substitute `0`                   | Worst option; distorts distribution |
+----------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
| **Probabilistic substitution** ✓ | Defensible                          |
+----------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
:::
:::

## NDInd Flag System

We attach a **Non-Detect Indicator** (`NDInd`) to every sample:

+-------------+-------------------------+---------------------------------+--------------+
| `NDInd`     | Meaning                 | Value action                    | Plot         |
+:===========:+=========================+=================================+:============:+
| `0`         | Detected above LOD      | Kept as-is                      | Normal point |
+-------------+-------------------------+---------------------------------+--------------+
| `1`         | Below LOD, above LOD/2  | Kept as-is                      | ○ circled    |
+-------------+-------------------------+---------------------------------+--------------+
| `2`         | Below LOD/2 but above 0 | **Replaced** with U(LOD/2, LOD) | ○ circled    |
+-------------+-------------------------+---------------------------------+--------------+
| `3`         | Exact zero              | **Replaced** with U(LOD/2, LOD) | ○ circled    |
+-------------+-------------------------+---------------------------------+--------------+

::: callout-important
Codes `1`, `2`, and `3` are **all circled on the final plot** so the we can see where censored data drives the trend.
:::

## `handle_nondetects()` — Full Function

```{r}
#| label: fn-nondetects-appendix

handle_nondetects <- function(df,
                              copies_col = "copies",    # name of the concentration column
                              lod_col    = "Detection", # name of the per-sample LOD column
                              seed       = 2020061) {   # fixed seed → reproducibility

  set.seed(seed)
  copies <- df[[copies_col]]
  lod    <- df[[lod_col]]

  zeroindex   <- copies == 0
  naindex     <- copies < lod;       naindex[is.na(naindex)]     <- TRUE
  naindex_hlf <- copies < lod * 0.5; naindex_hlf[is.na(naindex_hlf)] <- TRUE

  df$rfill <- 0; df$NDInd <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(df)))
    df$rfill[i] <- runif(1, lod[i] / 2, lod[i])

  df[[copies_col]][naindex_hlf] <- df$rfill[naindex_hlf]
  df$NDInd[naindex]     <- 1L
  df$NDInd[naindex_hlf] <- 2L
  df$NDInd[zeroindex]   <- 3L
  return(df)
}
```
